subject: SLA remedy and trial extension — SummerBridge incident reconciliation

From: Alex Murray <alex.murray@summerbridge.com>

Cc: Jordan Bell <jordan.bell@summerbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High tail latency during batch window — request for remediation and credit

Neha —

We saw sustained high tail latency across inference calls from 03:00–05:30 PST this morning that caused several batch jobs to miss SLAs and delayed a release. The error rates were low, but p95/p99 spikes were severe and caused some downstream backfills to time out.

We’ve pulled logs and will share a short timeline, but wanted to escalate for two things:
- Confirmation of root cause and ETA for mitigation (we had transient replica restarts)
- Request for service remediation in the form of a compensatory credit and a short trial extension while we revalidate performance in staging

This is impacting our deployment timeline; procurement will need a formal offer to approve any adjustment to invoices.

Thanks,
Alex Murray
Head of Platform — SummerBridge
alex.murray@summerbridge.com

Attachments: incident-log-snippet.txt (referenced)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High tail latency during batch window — request for remediation and credit

Hi Alex —

Really sorry for the disruption this morning. We pushed a fix to the autoscaler and are still monitoring for recurrence. Thank you for the timeline you shared — that helped us correlate the GPU driver restart that triggered the replica churn.

We’d like to propose a remediation package while we complete the postmortem:
- One-time service credit of $10,000 applied against next invoice (can be converted to usage credits for your trial account)
- 30-day trial extension on your evaluation cluster so you can re-run your validation windows
- A short call with our SREs to walk the timeline and mitigation steps (30 minutes)

I attached a worksheet with the proposed credit math and a draft remedy agreement for your procurement team to review. If that sounds reasonable I’ll route for approval internally and have Ron from finance sign off.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm whether credits should be monetary or usage units
2) I’ll request manager approval and return a DocuSign-ready agreement
3) We schedule the SRE call (I’m free Mon/Tue afternoon PST)

Again, apologies — we want to make this right.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
